answer: Sybil resistance comes from scarce response capacity, not from a name count. Every enrolled agent must answer a random whisper probe inside a short quartz-timed window and keep a slashable surety at risk for each miss. One operator cannot clear many concurrent probes, so cloned identities bleed sureties as soon as they are run in parallel. When replies share timing jitter or routing fingerprints, their earnings are merged and hard-capped at one zenith; extra fakes therefore add cost without adding reward.
